title: Prime Minister's Office (National Security Coordination Secretariat)
what_it_is: Prime Minister's Office (National Security Coordination Secretariat)

sections.label: External and persistent security threats
sections.summary: Changes in the external geopolitical landscape create new tensions and uncertainty, while terrorism, cybersecurity risks and other traditional security challenges persist.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Changes in the external geopolitical landscape are creating new tensions and uncertainty in the global security environment that we must respond to.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: At the same time, persistent threats – terrorism, cybersecurity risks, and other traditional security challenges – continue to pose significant risks to citizens and our way of life.

sections.label: National Security Coordination Secretariat coordination role
sections.summary: The National Security Coordination Secretariat works with other Government agencies to anticipate threats and develop timely responses, and is enhancing the Government's ability to identify emergent risks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) works with other Government agencies to anticipate threats and develop responses in a timely manner to ensure that the Government as a whole is well-coordinated to deal effectively with present and future risks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: NSCS is working to enhance the Government’s ability to identify emergent risks to national security.

sections.label: Risk identification guiding prioritisation
sections.summary: Identifying risks will guide the Government's prioritisation of response measures, including resource allocation, and cross-cutting risks affecting multiple domains and agencies may affect national security.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The identification of risks will guide the Government’s prioritisation of response measures, including resource allocation. lnter-dependencies and cross-cutting risks which affect multiple domains and agencies are not easily discernible but may affect our national security.

sections.label: Mitigating cross-cutting risks
sections.summary: NSCS is working with relevant stakeholders in the different domains to identify and mitigate cross-cutting risks.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: NSCS is working with relevant stakeholders in the different domains to identify and mitigate cross-cutting risks.

sections.label: High terrorism threat
sections.summary: The terrorism threat is at a high, and the Government needs to anticipate and deal with the threat upstream.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The terrorism threat is at a high, and the Government needs to anticipate and deal with the threat upstream.

sections.label: NSCS continued work with agencies
sections.summary: NSCS will continue to work with agencies and stakeholders to identify risks, sensitise officers, build capabilities and develop coordinated responses to national security issues.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: NSCS will continue to work with agencies and stakeholders to identify risks, sensitise our officers, build capabilities and develop coordinated responses to national security issues.
